newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end strong, seen still bullish.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end strong, seen still bullish.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares rose about one percent on Friday and brokers said they expected them to continue strong next week on increased liquidity in the equity market.
The key industrial index leapt 118.09 points -- or 1.1 percent -- to close at 10,825.02. It surged 437.22 points on the week.
"There's a lot of money out there looking for a home in the equity market and we expect liquidity to increase next week as people get their refunds from the Dairibord offer," one broker said.
The Dairibord of Zimbabwe Limited offer, which closed last Friday, is the government's first public offer of a state firm under a longstanding privatisation programme.
The offer, which has seen the government cutting its stake in the national dairy from 100 percent to 25 percent, was 10 times oversubscribed.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Friday, pharmaceutical group Caps leapt 200 cents to 3,000, bankers Barclays jumped 120 cents to 3,500, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans rose 100 cents to 4,100 and finance house Finhold gained 90 cents to 600.

Tyre re-processor and rubber products-maker NTS and merchant banker NMB each traded 50 cents up at 390 and 3,400 respectively, tea producer Tanganda rose 40 cents to 800, and blue-chip supermarkets, hotels and beverages conglomerate Delta gained 30 cents to 1,800.
Against the trend, finance house UDC dropped 15 cents to 260, cable manufacturer BICAF shed 10 cents to 320 and publishing group Zimpapers eased two cents to 115.
Minings were also fairly active in small volumes in gold counters despite bullion's drop to a 12-year low fix in London on Friday.
Gold producer Ashanti Zimbabwe Depositary Receipts added five cents to 115 and Wankie Colliery.
But Falgold eased four cents to 66 and nickel giant Bindura lost 10 cents to 620, dragging the mining index 4.23 points down to 867.19.
The index dropped 62.42 points on the week.
